comment: Brief 183 — the JakeTunes scheduler manifest. Every launchd job the pipeline depends on, in git: managed jobs render from templates/ via install-launchagents.sh (dry-run by default); existing-plist jobs already live in the repo as loose plists and are listed for completeness; external jobs are NOT defined in this repo and are listed so the manifest is the whole truth — their schedules are never invented here. 'proposed: true' marks a schedule this manifest newly proposes (the job or its timing was not previously defined in the repo).

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.brain-trainer
jobs.machine: homemini (state host; trainer header: state on the Mini / NAS canonical)
jobs.notes: 02:00 is evidenced in the trainer's own header comments (BRAIN_MINUTES note: 'the trainer (02:00) is always finished well before brain-improve (03:05)'). No plist for this job existed in the repo before this manifest — the label and template here are the new canonical definition. Status written by the trainer via scripts/brain-status.mjs (Brief 176).

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.brain-watchdog
jobs.notes: Brief 176 created the watchdog and assigned its launchd template to this manifest. Hourly is proposed: the watchdog alerts when brain-status.json is >26h old (or missing/corrupt), so an hourly check bounds the alert lag to ~1h. Exits 1 while stale — that non-zero exit in launchd's list is expected, not a failure of the agent itself.

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.taxonomy
jobs.machine: app host (the machine whose state dir holds metadata-overrides.json)
jobs.notes: The taxonomy job's existence is evidenced (scripts/taxonomy-classify.py runs nightly and defers when the app is running) but no schedule or label for it exists in the repo — 01:30 and this label are proposed (before the 02:00 trainer, so fresh subgenres fold into the night's training; the script also triggers its own --reembed-all after a write). Status = the Brief 182 deferral marker: present means writes are owed.

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.taste-eval
jobs.notes: RETIRED 2026-10-19 (taste-engine repairs): it actually ran on the LAPTOP every 3 days against the laptop's copy of the brain, which stopped updating in August once homemini took over the brain; it timed out on 10/17. The homemini weekly brain eval (JakeTunesMobile deploy/brain-eval-weekly.sh -> /api/brain-eval, Fridays 08:30) measures the same taste AUC on the canonical library, and the nightly taste engine now measures taste on held-back behavior. Laptop plist kept as com.jaketunes.taste-eval.plist.retired-20261019.

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.enrichment-catchup
jobs.notes: Brief 177's catch-up driver. INSTALLED 2026-10-20 on the laptop (lyrics.json and the CLAP index had both stopped on 9/1: this job was proposed here and never installed). 04:30 daily, after the 04:00 listening-history job. The wrapper runs origin/main's scripts from its own worktree (never the shared checkout) and skips the CLAP phase while JakeTunes is playing audio. Install this one plist: install-launchagents.sh --apply --only com.jaketunes.enrichment-catchup. Cap comes from clap-probe.json when the probe has been run on the machine (manual step, Brief 177); otherwise the labelled UNMEASURED fallback (300).
jobs.program: bash ~/bin/jaketunes-enrichment-nightly.sh (scripts/launchd/enrichment-nightly.sh -> node scripts/enrichment-catchup.mjs --budget-min 60, from its own origin/main worktree)

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.dev-mirror
jobs.notes: Already versioned as a loose plist in scripts/. Not rendered by the installer (it predates this manifest and has its own install path); listed so the manifest covers every job.

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.listening-history
jobs.notes: Already versioned as a loose plist in scripts/ (installed as ~/bin/jaketunes-listening-history.sh on homemini). Not rendered by the installer.

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.scotus-backup
jobs.notes: Already versioned as a loose plist in scripts/. Not rendered by the installer.

jobs.label: brain-improve
jobs.notes: Its TIME is evidenced — brain-trainer.mjs: 'the trainer (02:00) is always finished well before brain-improve (03:05)' — and docs/brain-improvement-2026h2.md discusses it, but no script or plist for it exists in this repo. Listed as external: the manifest records that it exists and when it runs; its definition lives wherever it was installed from, and is NOT invented here.

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.sync
jobs.notes: SUPERSEDED — do not install. Per src/main/sync-orchestrator.ts's header: the launchd job could not access /Volumes/JakeShared on macOS Sequoia (launchd-domain processes are blocked from network volumes regardless of TCC grants), so the app's main process replaced launchd as the trigger. The script it ran (~/bin/jaketunes-homemini-sync.sh, a copy of 'Dr. Claude/scripts/jaketunes-homemini-sync.sh') is still the sync engine — Brief 183 adds a startup drift check comparing the installed copy against the repo copy. Listed so nobody resurrects the agent from the script's stale header.
jobs.schedule: was every 600s (evidenced in the sync script's header)

jobs.label: com.jaketunes.taste-engine
jobs.notes: 2026-10-19 taste-engine program: the nightly taste-learning exercise (scripts/taste-engine-nightly.sh -> scripts/taste-engine.py). 04:40, after the 04:00 listening history it reads; runs from the ~/JakeTunesV3-yir detached origin/main checkout that job refreshes, so only merged code runs (render with JAKETUNES_REPO_DIR=~/JakeTunesV3-yir; install this one plist, not --apply on everything). Publishes taste-state.json to ~/JakeTunesState + the NAS. Watched both ways: it fails loudly if the history is >30h old, and the 04:00 job alerts if this job's status is >30h old.
